name: BoolODE
simulation_summary: Converts Boolean regulatory models to stochastic differential equations and exports sampled expression trajectories. Native topology is retained; regulatory signs are conservatively derived from Boolean negation scope. Group networks repeat the fixed global graph rather than model regulatory rewiring.

optional.usage: Wrapper copies this file into BoolODE model_dir and sets jobs[].model_initial_conditions when mounted; bundled presets use their pinned repository initial-condition files when available.
Wrapper copies this file into BoolODE model_dir and sets jobs[].interaction_strengths when mounted; bundled presets use their pinned repository interaction-strength files when available.

conditional_required.usage: Wrapper copies this BoolODE Gene/Rule table into model_dir and sets jobs[].model_definition when model_preset=custom_files. Empty values and pandas missing-value tokens such as NA, NaN or NULL are rejected because the pinned upstream parser does not preserve them as identifiers.

compatibility_rules.message: Group truth requires n_clusters >= 2 so BoolODE produces trajectory cluster IDs for public groups and group truth contexts.

BoolODE's nClusters>1 trajectory-clustering path requires sample_cells=false; sample_cells=true writes only one sampled cell per trajectory and does not populate the full trajectories needed by ClusterIds.csv.

threading.upstream_mapping: The reviewed BoolODE YAML exposes only a do_parallel boolean; the pinned implementation calls multiprocessing.Pool() without a process-count argument and hard-codes KMeans n_jobs=8. The wrapper therefore rejects runtime_resources.threads != 1, writes do_parallel=false, and patches the imported public BoolODE KMeans constructor to n_jobs=1 before calling BoolODE.ConfigParser.parse(...).execute_jobs().

model_preset.description: Selects a bundled BoolODE Boolean model from the pinned upstream repository or mounted custom BoolODE-format files.

model_type.description: Maps to global_settings.modeltype and controls whether BoolODE uses Hill-function or soft-Heaviside regulatory terms.

simulation_time.description: Maps to jobs[].simulation_time, the maximum simulated trajectory time. Integral values are serialized as YAML integers because the pinned BoolODE implementation uses range(1, tmax*100) when the full trajectory output has at least 1000 columns. ANDREA and the wrapper reject non-integral values in that branch.

num_cells.description: Maps to jobs[].num_cells. BoolODE runs this many stochastic trajectories and may sample one expression cell from each trajectory when the full trajectory matrix is large.

n_clusters.description: Maps to jobs[].nClusters. Values greater than one make BoolODE cluster full simulated trajectories and emit ClusterIds.csv.

sample_cells.description: Maps to jobs[].sample_cells. When true, BoolODE samples one time point from each trajectory during simulation; this requires n_clusters=1 and num_cells<1000 in the pinned implementation.

sample_parameters.description: Maps to jobs[].sample_pars, causing BoolODE to sample kinetic parameters around defaults instead of fixing them exactly.

sample_std.description: Maps to jobs[].sample_std, the relative standard deviation used when sample_parameters=true.

identical_parameters.description: Maps to jobs[].identical_pars, making BoolODE reuse one sampled kinetic value per parameter class when sample_parameters=true.

integration_step_size.description: Maps to jobs[].integration_step_size and controls the ODE simulation time grid. With sample_cells=false, the full output has num_cells * (int(simulation_time / integration_step_size) - 1) columns. At 1000 or more columns upstream resamples indices up to simulation_time*100-1, requiring integration_step_size<=0.01 and integral simulation_time. The default 0.01 is recommended; smaller steps retain upstream's fixed index-sampling range. At least three time points are required in all cases.

dropout.description: Serializable BoolODE dropout post-processing controls. When enabled, expression.tsv uses the dropout-processed ExpressionData.csv and clean expression is preserved under provenance/raw/.

enabled.description: Whether to run BoolODE's dropout induction post-processing.

drop_cutoff.description: Expression quantile below which values are eligible for dropout.

drop_prob.description: Probability of setting an eligible expression value to zero.

upstream_configuration: global_settings.do_simulations=true with jobs[].model_definition set to a bundled or mounted BoolODE Boolean model.
BoolODE run_experiment.startRun() calls utils.generateInputFiles(), which writes refNetwork.csv from the Boolean rules.
truth_contexts.generation: Retain native non-self refNetwork.csv topology and derive signs from the corresponding Boolean rule: and/or preserve polarity, not reverses it. Mixed-polarity or unparsed regulator occurrences have sign ?; the native CSV is preserved unchanged.
truth_contexts.score_semantics: score=1.0. Signs are Boolean literal polarities with correct nested-negation scope, not the upstream first-not heuristic; mixed polarity or unsupported syntax gives sign ?. No kinetic effect magnitude is claimed.
limitations: Complex Boolean logic is projected to pairwise edges; native topology is retained and signs are derived conservatively from the input rules.
Interaction-strength input files affect ODE thresholds but are not represented as public truth scores because refNetwork.csv does not emit magnitudes.

A syntactic edge may be logically redundant; mixed-polarity rules do not establish a globally monotone regulatory effect. Upstream simulation seeds individual trajectories by trajectory index, so changing the run seed does not guarantee independent stochastic trajectories.

truth_contexts.explanation: The global-truth capability does not export group truth contexts.
BoolODE does not expose cell-specific regulatory networks.

derivations.method: Export every public gene identifier present in expression.tsv as extras/enrichment_background.txt, one gene per line.
assumptions: The generated expression feature set is the appropriate enrichment background for downstream analysis of the simulated dataset.
limitations: The background is synthetic and dataset-derived, not an organism-specific external annotation universe.

derivations.method: Export the normalized global truth edges, including corrected Boolean-polarity signs, as an oracle prior; for prior_grn_by_group repeat those fixed edges under each public group identifier.
assumptions: BoolODE's native reference network can serve as an oracle structural prior when explicitly requested.
limitations: This is a truth-derived oracle prior rather than an independently noisy prior.
Edge magnitudes are unavailable in refNetwork.csv and are therefore binary.

derivations.method: Export the unique Gene1 regulator identifiers from refNetwork.csv, one per line, after applying the same public gene-id normalization used for expression.tsv and truth/networks.csv.
assumptions: BoolODE is designed for transcription factor regulatory networks, so native refNetwork.csv regulators define the simulated TF/regulator universe.
limitations: The TF list reflects simulator regulators, not an external organism-specific TF catalogue.

derivations.method: Preserve upstream directed non-self topology; parse Boolean and/or/not syntax to assign regulator polarity, with ? for mixed or unsupported polarity.
assumptions: Consistent literal polarity implies a monotone Boolean influence when that regulator affects the rule.
limitations: No truth-table simplification or kinetic effect-size estimation is performed; native refNetwork.csv signs remain archived for inspection.

derivations.method: For each expression cell column, parse the native E<experiment>_<time> identifier, join E<experiment> to ClusterIds.csv, and emit a stable public group label cluster_<label> in extras/groups.tsv.
assumptions: BoolODE ClusterIds.csv assigns each simulated trajectory to the cluster used by the paper as a column group or steady-state trajectory label.
Every public expression column retains an experiment prefix that can be joined back to ClusterIds.csv.
limitations: Groups are k-means trajectory clusters, not curated biological annotations.
K-means numeric cluster labels are arbitrary across runs.

derivations.method: Reuse each cell's public group as its phenotype label and order phenotypes by mean native simulation Time across cells in that group, resolving ties by group id.
assumptions: Trajectory clusters provide a useful synthetic phenotype label for grouped BoolODE benchmarks.
Mean simulation time provides a deterministic ordering hint even though BoolODE does not emit a lineage tree.
limitations: The phenotype label is a cluster label, not a curated cell type name.
Ordering by mean time is descriptive and does not imply parent-child lineage relations.

derivations.method: Export one row per observed group with cluster_id equal to the public group id, annotation equal to the same id, and optional order inherited from the column_phenotypes group order.
assumptions: BoolODE's trajectory clusters are the most stable public identities available for grouped synthetic data.
limitations: Annotations are synthetic cluster identifiers rather than biological cell-type names.

limitations: This is a truth-derived oracle prior and does not encode group-varying regulation.
Benchmarks using prior_grn_by_group with BoolODE should account for the fixed topology across groups.

derivations.method: For every group emitted in groups.tsv, duplicate the fixed BoolODE global truth GRN into context=group:<group_id> rows in truth/networks.csv.
assumptions: A grouped benchmark can explicitly represent BoolODE's fixed-GRN design by providing one identical group context per trajectory cluster.
This satisfies the cumulative grouped truth contract without pretending that BoolODE models group-specific GRN rewiring.
limitations: Group truth networks are wrapper-derived context expansions, not native BoolODE group-specific network outputs.
All group truth contexts are identical except for their context labels.
